Settings goes back to being a window of its own, and the home screen now arrives instead of appearing all at once.

## Settings is a separate window again

The shell rework in v0.22.0 turned Settings into a page inside the main window, which meant changing one knob navigated the app away from whatever you were looking at — and the gear ended up in two places.

- Settings opens as its own window from anywhere in the app, so it never takes the screen away from a live meeting. It is no longer disabled while recording.
- The title bar gear is the single entry point; the duplicate row at the bottom of the sidebar is gone.
- Deep links still land where they should: the 🌐 menu's "translation settings" opens the translation panel, whether the window is already open or not.

## A gentler home screen

The overview now fades up in reading order — start, then intel that needs attention, then recent recordings, with the recent rows cascading in. Turning on "reduce motion" in macOS disables the animation entirely.

## Fixes

- The microphone level meter could leave a listener behind when it was torn down mid-setup — switching input devices quickly, or opening and closing the meter repeatedly, slowly piled up dead listeners.
